correctness.rationale: PASS: The Q-sector is two-dimensional. Diagonalizing the three-site Hamiltonians at fluxes 0 and pi/3 yields Q-restricted factors A=I+(a-1)P0 and B=I+(conjugate(a)-1)P1, a=(1+2 exp(3iJtau))/3, with |<v0,v1>|^2=1/4. Their product C=BA has det(C†C)=t² and tr(C†C)=2t+(1-t)²/4, hence singular values [sqrt(16t+(1-t)^2)±(1-t)]/4, t=(5+4cos(3Jtau))/9. The larger c(t) is strictly increasing in t since (t+7)^2-(t²+14t+1)=48. Thus c<1 except exact revival t=1, geometrically controls survival for every off-target pure initial state. The minimum at t=1/9 (z=-1) yields 1-((2+sqrt13)/9)^2=(64-4sqrt13)/81. At this point tr C=-2/9, det C=1/9, eigenvalues (-1±2i sqrt2)/9 and rho=1/3; det gives rho(C)>=sqrt(t)>=1/3 globally. Independent checks directly exponentiated the full 3x3 Hamiltonians at 104 intervals and checked the 2x2 singular norm. This is all-tau analytical proof, not a finite-sample inference.
